title: Auth request headers
topic: Spreading `BASE_OPTS` and `BASE_OPTS.headers` without leaking auth tokens
blurb: A JS helper building per-request headers from a shared base config.
prompt: Spec: build per-request options from `BASE_OPTS`, adding `authorization` when `token` is truthy, without mutating `BASE_OPTS` or its `headers`. Review this helper — tap a line if it breaks the spec, or let it pass.
conclusion: AI summary: Clones `headers` separately and overrides it in the returned copy, so `BASE_OPTS.headers` never picks up a user's token.

diagnosis: `BASE_OPTS` is declared with `const`, which freezes nested `headers` and makes line 4 throw TypeError.
Using lowercase `accept` instead of `Accept` causes `headers` spread to drop the key.
Putting `BASE_OPTS` at module scope means every call shares the exact same `timeout` and `headers` reference.
Missing `Object.freeze` on `BASE_OPTS` means line 3 still mutates it.
fix: Change `const BASE_OPTS` to `let BASE_OPTS` so copies can be modified.
Move `BASE_OPTS` inside `buildRequestOpts` so it's rebuilt on every call.
Wrap `BASE_OPTS` in `Object.freeze(...)` to block nested writes.
Store `headers` as a `Map` instead of a plain object.

diagnosis: Missing default `token = ""` causes `if (token)` on line 4 to throw ReferenceError when called with no args.
Accepting `token` without trimming lets whitespace tokens bypass the `if` guard and mutate `BASE_OPTS`.
`buildRequestOpts` isn't `async`, so it can't return request options for `fetch`.
Parameter `token` shadows a global browser property.
fix: Default the parameter to `token = null` so zero-arg calls don't throw.
Rename `token` to `authToken` to avoid shadowing.
Mark the function `async` for `fetch` callers.
Validate `typeof token === 'string'` before reading `BASE_OPTS`.

diagnosis: Object spread `{ ...BASE_OPTS.headers }` is a shallow copy, so `headers` still points to `BASE_OPTS.headers` and line 4 mutates the global default.
Declaring `const headers` prevents line 4 from adding the `authorization` property.
Spreading `BASE_OPTS.headers` loses `timeout: 2000` from the final options object.
Spreading a nested property throws TypeError unless `BASE_OPTS` is spread first.
fix: Use `structuredClone(BASE_OPTS.headers)` because `{ ...obj }` shares the same reference.
Change `const headers` to `let headers` so line 4 can assign `authorization`.
Spread `{ ...BASE_OPTS }` first on line 3 instead of `BASE_OPTS.headers`.
Use `Object.assign(BASE_OPTS.headers, {})` to clone safely.

diagnosis: Assigning `headers.authorization` mutates `BASE_OPTS.headers`, leaking the Bearer token to the next anonymous call.
Missing curly braces around the `if` body causes line 5 to only run when `token` is truthy.
Template literal `` `Bearer ${token}` `` leaves `${token}` uninterpolated because of backticks.
If `token` is empty, `headers.authorization` stays set from the previous call.
fix: Delete `headers.authorization` in an `else` branch so anonymous calls don't inherit it.
Wrap the `if` body in `{ ... }` so `return` always runs.
Replace the template literal with `'Bearer ' + token`.
Build a second clone `{ ...headers, authorization: ... }` on line 4.

diagnosis: Shallow copy bug: `{ ...BASE_OPTS, headers }` copies `BASE_OPTS.headers` *over* the local `headers`, wiping out `authorization`.
Shorthand `headers` puts `{ headers: { headers: ... } }` nested one level too deep.
Spreading `BASE_OPTS` first shares `BASE_OPTS.headers` between the returned object and the global default.
Missing `timeout` in the shorthand means `timeout` is dropped when `headers` is supplied.
fix: Put `headers` before `...BASE_OPTS`: `return { headers, ...BASE_OPTS };`.
Write `headers: { ...headers }` explicitly instead of shorthand `headers`.
Use `Object.assign(BASE_OPTS, { headers })` instead of object spread.
Write `{ timeout: BASE_OPTS.timeout, headers }` so `BASE_OPTS` isn't spread.

diagnosis: Missing semicolon after the function block causes syntax errors in strict mode.
The function leaks `headers` into the outer scope after returning.
Calling `buildRequestOpts()` twice returns the exact same object identity.
Nothing resets `BASE_OPTS.headers` before the function closes.
fix: Reset `delete BASE_OPTS.headers.authorization;` before returning.
Add `};` at the end of the function declaration.
Wrap the returned object in `structuredClone(...)`.
Return `Object.freeze(...)` so callers can't mutate it.

clean_conclusion: This one actually clones the nested object: line 3 builds a fresh `headers` copy before setting `authorization`, and line 5's `headers` comes *after* `...BASE_OPTS` so it overrides cleanly — `BASE_OPTS` stays untouched.
explanation: This one actually clones the nested object: line 3 builds a fresh `headers` copy before setting `authorization`, and line 5's `headers` comes *after* `...BASE_OPTS` so it overrides cleanly — `BASE_OPTS` stays untouched.
